sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Corporate Scope 1-3 Carbon Footprint Auditing and Offset Brokerage

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaty with the People's Republic of China (in force)
BLEU Bilateral Investment Treaty with the Republic of Korea (in force)
Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement between Luxembourg and the United States of America (in force, as amended)
Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement between Luxembourg and the Federal Republic of Germany (in force)
Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (MLI), ratified by Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), as amended by AMLD5 implementing legislation; Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 sur les sociétés commerciales, including the SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on internal governance and AML/CFT, as amended; applicable grand-ducal implementing regulations of the RBE.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport of each natural person general partner and each beneficial owner holding 25% or more of the partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport authority of the country of residence (civil registrar or police issuing office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the country is an HCCH Apostille Convention member; otherwise Consular Legalization by the Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and extract of the register of directors/shareholders of any corporate general partner or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or company registrar of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Apostille countries, Consular Legalization by the competent Luxembourg diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft limited partnership agreement (SCSp) and notarially certified power of attorney for the appointed Luxembourg registered agent or incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction where the power of attorney is executed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, depending on the country of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered office consent in Luxembourg, such as lease agreement or written landlord consent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg registered office provider or lessor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required if issued in Luxembourg; notarized if executed outside Luxembourg

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of wealth and source of funds declaration, together with independent bank reference letter for each beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution or accredited private bank holding the relevant account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization unless issued by an EEA bank subject to EU AML/CFT supervision

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all general partners, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated List, EU Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, and Luxembourg domestic administrative sanctions registries. PEP status must be determined using a reliable independent commercial database and verified by documentary evidence. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, family member, or close associate, including senior management approval, written source-of-wealth analysis, transaction monitoring, and annual re-screening. Results must be documented in the AML file and made available to the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF) and the CSSF upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) electronic filing portal, accessible via lbr.lu (eJustice / MyLBR electronic filing).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company and partnership names must be in Latin script; non-Latin script names are transliterated into Roman characters at the discretion of the RCS. The name must be grammatically correct, not misleading, and compatible with the partnership's legal form. The SCSp designation must appear in the name as 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'. Names in French, German, English, or Luxembourgish are normally acceptable if rendered in Latin characters.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de commerce / Chamber of Commerce
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed for successive 90-day periods by filing a renewal request before expiration. If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant may request internal reconsideration within one month by email or through the lbr.lu portal, attaching the rejection notice and evidence of non-conflicting use. If the RCS maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Commercial Chamber) through a Luxembourg-qualified avocat, within one month of notification. The appeal must state the proposed name, the RCS decision, and the grounds on which the name is not contrary to public policy, mandatory legal-form rules, or prior-registered rights. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a revised name without prejudice; prior rejection does not create a bar to a different compliant name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable for RCS registration and mail-handling purposes provided the SCSp maintains a registered office address in Luxembourg and the general partner or a designated Luxembourg-based agent can receive official notifications. For an ESG/carbon accounting advisory and offset brokerage activity, a pure virtual office may be tolerated at formation, but robust commercial substance is strongly recommended: adequate Luxembourg premises, local decision-making records, personnel, and bank accounts in Luxembourg become necessary if the entity seeks recognition under Luxembourg tax treaty provisions, claims tax residence, or wishes to avoid challenge as a letter-box or economically artificial arrangement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 10-15% per year for an unregulated professional-services partnership. The risk increases to 25-30% where the SCSp files for treaty benefits, engages in intra-group financing or passes substantial revenue as brokerage commission, or where the general partner is a corporate vehicle in a non-cooperative jurisdiction. Unannounced physical inspections by the RCS, the trade inspectorate, or the Luxembourg tax authorities are possible if there is reasonable suspicion of false registered office data or artificial substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and issuance of non-registration certificate with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
Initial electronic filing of the SCSp incorporation document and RCS publication of incorporation
Notarial certification of the SCSp partnership agreement and related signatures, if notarial form is elected or required by the transaction docs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff and prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, or consular legalization of foreign passport copies, corporate extracts, powers of attorney, and source-of-funds documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / competent apostille authority in the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention tariff or consular fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the SCSp limited partnership agreement, internal governance documentation, and incorporation filing assistance by a Luxembourg law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (avocat à la Cour)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for corporate formation work

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner registration and UBO declaration filing with the Luxembourg RBE register
AML/CFT customer due diligence, PEP identification, OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening, and risk assessment file preparation for all UBOs and general partners
Registered office services for the first 12 months, including physical Luxembourg address, mail handling, and official correspondence routing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate service provider (Professional of the Financial Sector or registered agent)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax registration review, confirmation of pass-through status, and issuance of tax clearance instructions for the newly formed SCSp

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Luxembourg Law of 11 July 2013 creating the société en commandite spéciale (SCSp); applicable provisions on partnerships and special limited partnerships set forth in Articles 1, 13, 101-108 and 109-132.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), under the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutional contract (contrat de société) in private written or notarial form, together with the RCS registration declaration for an SCSp and the mandatory publication in the electronic compendium of legal entities (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations - RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SCSp has no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no mandatory escrow account. Contributions are fixed freely in the partnership agreement and may be made in cash, in kind, or as industry, provided they are actually and irrevocably made as agreed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED BY THE SOLE MANAGER OF __SCSP__ ACTING ON BEHALF OF THE PARTNERSHIP THAT: (1) the initial capital contribution plan is adopted; each partner subscribes to the partnership interests set out in Schedule I and contributes the assets described therein; (2) the registered office of the SCSp is fixed at __ADDRESS__, Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; (3) __NAME__ is appointed as Manager of the SCSp, with full signatory authority for all banking, RCS, VAT and tax filings; (4) the Manager is directed to file the articles of association with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, arrange RESA publication, complete UBO registration, and open corporate bank accounts. This resolution is valid from the date of signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability check and partnership agreement drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and RCS name reservation desk via lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the proposed corporate name against the RCS database, reserve the chosen name, and draft the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société). The agreement must state the legal form, commercial object, corporate name, registered office address, partner contributions, management powers, profit-sharing arrangement and transfer rules. For an SCSp, a notarial deed is optional unless a real estate contribution is made, but all partners must sign the agreement.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and reservation receipt
Passport or civil status data of all general and limited partners
If a legal entity is a partner, extract from its trade register and authority documents
Draft partnership agreement
Signed powers of attorney for any representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, modify the distinguishing element and resubmit the reservation application. If the RCS or notary raises concerns on the object or governance clauses, amend the partnership agreement and resubmit for approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarisation of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public, or direct execution by partners for private deed SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalise and execute the constitutional contract. If the SCSp uses a private deed, all partners must sign and the signatures should be legalised where required by foreign parties. If notarial form is selected, the scroll is signed before a Luxembourg notary who will retain the original and issue notarial copies. Confirm the registered office address and final schedules of contributions before signature.
required_dossiers: Final partnership agreement
Schedule of contributions and valuation statements for in-kind contributions
Proof of registered office availability (lease letter, sublease consent or address agreement)
Notarial deed, if applicable
Passport copies and if requested, residence or employment data for the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner refuses to sign or incomplete data is identified, execute a rectifying deed or additional deed before the notary prior to RCS registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS registration declaration for an SCSp, together with the signed constitutional contract and statutory particulars. Include the name, object, registered office, duration, trade names, general partner identity, managers, subscription and contribution amounts, and the date of execution. Pay the official registration fee. Once the registration is accepted, the RCS publishes a legal notice in RESA.
required_dossiers: RCS SCSp declaration form
Signed partnership agreement or notarial deed
Extract of criminal record (bulletin no. 3) for each manager
Identity and proof of authority of the filing agent
Declaration of non-bankruptcy and honour statement, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, provide the requested clarifications or amended documents within the stated deadline. If registration is refused without valid grounds, an appeal is available before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UBO filing and tax, VAT and social security registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS UBO Register; Luxembourg Inland Revenue (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) via guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the UBO declaration with the RCS within 30 days of incorporation, identifying all beneficial owners and the nature of their interest. Apply to the Luxembourg Inland Revenue for the direct tax identification number and, if applicable, net wealth tax reference. Register for VAT with the AEDT if the carbon accounting and offset brokerage activity is within the scope of Luxembourg VAT, and register with the CCSS only if the partnership later hires employees.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of incorporation and commercial register extract
UBO declaration (Form T/UBO)
Completed tax registration questionnaire
Partnership agreement and RCS publication notice
Personal identification data of managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UBO declaration is queried, complete the beneficial ownership data and resubmit within the RCS deadline. For tax registrations, supply the additional documentary evidence requested by the ACD or AEDT via eSpace or postal filing before any enforcement measure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and AML/KYC confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Credit institution in Luxembourg supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the SCSp constitutional documents, RCS extract, UBO registration proof, beneficial ownership chart, source of funds, commercial business plan, and identification of partners to the selected bank. Complete the bank's know-your-customer process and ensure the bank mandates the SWIFT wire payment rails required for the carbon advisory and offset brokerage services.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the partnership agreement
RCS registration extract
UBO certificate or RCS UBO extract
Passport and proof of address of each manager and partner
Business plan and source of funds questionnaire
Bank account opening and AML forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional AML information, provide corporate structure charts, bank references or supportable source-of-wealth evidence. If the application is rejected, the applicant may submit a complete application to another CSSF-supervised institution or contact the Luxembourg financial ombudsman in accordance with banking complaints procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered office installation and opening bookkeeping
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local commune for commercial premises; Luxembourg Inland Revenue (ACD) for bookkeeping compliance; RCS for registrable event updates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is physically available and operational, hold the minute book and capital contribution ledger, prepare the opening balance sheet according to Luxembourg generally accepted accounting principles, and perform the first annual control of partnership interests. Report any subsequent appointment of managers or change of registered office to the RCS within the statutory deadlines.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or registered office consent letter
Proof of utility and office equipment
Initial capital receipt statements or contribution records
Opening balance sheet preparation records
Partnership tax and accounting compliance calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commune or tax office questions the physical presence of the office, provide the lease agreement, utility bills and on-site evidence. If an RCS filing becomes necessary due to management changes, file the amendment promptly after receipt of the new manager's acceptance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial licensing authority is engaged for this office-based ESG and carbon accounting advisory service. If a local commercial registration formalities applies, the competent body is the commune in which the registered office is situated.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - ISIC 7020 management consultancy activities and offset brokerage services are not listed as regulated professions in Luxembourg. No industrial operating permit or regulated professional licence is required to carry out the carbon footprint audit and carbon offset advisory activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (AEV), Ministry of Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity is office-based and does not correspond to any project category listed under Luxembourg environmental impact assessment legislation. No EIA screening or full environmental impact report is required for an SCSp conducting corporate carbon auditing and offset brokerage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - the business generates no wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions, combustion exhaust or industrial waste requiring a discharge permit. Any conventional office waste handling must nevertheless comply with the Luxembourg law on waste and administrative requirements of the local commune.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required for ordinary office premises under the applicable municipal fire and building safety regulations, including adequate exit routes and portable extinguishers. Occupational health and safety clearance must comply with the Luxembourg Labour Code and the inspections of the Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines - ITM), covering electrical safety, workstation ergonomics and safe means of access. No civil defence or special anti-disaster clearance is applicable to a non-industrial consultancy operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Inland Revenue, for direct income taxes, partnership information returns and tax residency certificates (portal: myguichet.lu; eCDF online filing). Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Luxembourg Indirect Tax and Registration Authority, for VAT registration, VAT returns and refunds (portal: myguichet.lu and eTVA online filing). Business registration: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), with publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Appoint a Luxembourg registered office and a local authorised representative if the SCSp is managed by non-residents. 2) File the constitutive documents and partnership agreement with the RCS via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), obtain the RCS registration number and the RNPM (Registre National des Personnes Morales) validation; registration is mandatory for the SCSp even though it lacks legal personality. 3) Submit notarised or legalised statutes, identification documents of all partners (natural or legal persons), registered office proof, and a local representative mandate; the RCS number constitutes the national business identifier automatically notified to the AEDT and ACD. 4) For VAT: file Form 640 (demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) with the AEDT; a VAT identification number is issued from the first taxable economic activity. 5) For foreign non-established taxable persons with no local fixed establishment, VAT registration is required before any taxable transaction in Luxembourg unless the reverse charge applies; non-EU entities must appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative approved by the AEDT. 6) Apply separately to the ACD for a direct tax reference number and for the partnership information return file (form 550-series); the SCSp itself is not assessed to corporate income tax or municipal business tax, but a tax file is required to report distributive income to partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by statutory design (Law of 23 July 2016 on the SCSp; Article 1ter LIR): no check-the-box election exists; transparency is mandatory for Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (IBP) and net wealth tax (IFI) at entity level. Partners are subject to tax personally on their distributive share of Luxembourg and foreign-source income according to their residence status. Available elections and relevant mechanisms: (a) VAT grouping / assujetti unique election under Article 60 of the VAT Law, whereby the SCSp may join other Luxembourg established persons as a single taxable person with prior AEDT approval; (b) the small-enterprise franchise (Article 57 VAT Law) may be waived, or is lost automatically when turnover exceeds EUR 35,000; (c) designation in the partnership agreement of the profit-sharing and capital call rules to confirm Luxembourg tax attribution; (d) hybrid mismatch rules under Luxembourg's ATAD transposition (Law of 21 December 2017 and 2020 amendments) apply – partners must align the SCSp's transparent Luxembourg treatment with the foreign counterparty characterisation to avoid disallowed deductions; no elective opt-out from transparency is permitted. The SCSp may also elect optional Irish/English-style limited partnership clauses only to the extent the Luxembourg commercial law permits, without altering fiscal transparency.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA) under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 (as amended), implementing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (net of VAT) for Luxembourg-established small enterprises under Article 57 of the VAT Law (franchise). No registration threshold for non-established foreign taxable persons: registration is required from the first taxable transaction unless the reverse charge shifts liability to the Luxembourg customer. For intra-Community distance sales of goods and cross-border B2C telecommunications/broadcasting/digital services under the One Stop Shop (OSS): EUR 10,000 annual Union-wide threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, digital stamping, or mandatory API pre-clearance for standard B2B VAT invoices. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory via the PEPPOL network under the Law of 26 June 2023 transposing Directive 2014/55/EU. As of 2025, B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary in Luxembourg, with structured e-invoices compliant with EN 16931 accepted; Luxembourg is aligned with the EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) package, which will introduce mandatory structured e-invoicing and digital transaction reporting through a harmonised EU standard, expected for cross-border B2B transactions by 2030 and phased for domestic supplies thereafter. Taxpayers must ensure invoice authenticity, integrity and legibility, and retain all original invoices for at least 6 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% export VAT applies strictly to (a) supplies of goods physically dispatched or transported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU, under Article 42 of the VAT Law, supported by a customs export declaration; and (b) certain goods-related ancillary services (transport, freight, handling) directly connected to exported goods. For the SCSp's ESG carbon footprint auditing and offset brokerage services, zero-rating is not the applicable mechanism: B2B services supplied to non-EU recipients are outside Luxembourg VAT scope under the general place-of-supply rule (recipient's place of establishment), and B2C cross-border consultancy services are outside scope where the effective use and enjoyment occurs outside the EU. Emission allowances and carbon credits traded on the EU ETS or voluntarily are treated as supplies of services subject to the standard 17% VAT rate when supplied in Luxembourg territory; brokerage and intermediary services to EU B2B customers are subject to reverse charge, and to non-EU B2B customers are outside scope. Input VAT incurred by the SCSp on Luxembourg costs is recoverable via the periodic VAT return (established entities) or the 13th Directive electronic refund procedure (non-established entities, form 3582M).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD – Single Administrative Document / electronic ESAD) with MRN (Movement Reference Number)
Export clearance certificate (EX-1 copy) from Luxembourg Customs
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR road consignment note, signed and dated by consignee or carrier
Bank transfer evidence (Swift/Wire) and Inward Remittance Certificate where applicable
Transport contracts, insurance certificates and correspondence proving removal of goods from EU territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg statutes do not impose a general 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark functions as an administrative substance and benchmark indicator used by the AEDT and ACD to verify the economic reality of export transactions and transfer pricing alignment. Where export zero-rating is claimed without adequate documentary substantiation, the AEDT may retrospectively claw back the 0% rate, assess VAT at 17% with statutory late-payment interest (currently 0.8% per month of arrears), and impose administrative fines ranging from EUR 250 to EUR 250,000 for invoice and declaration violations under Articles 66-67 of the VAT Law. Fraudulent zero-rating claims or counterfeit export evidence constitute tax fraud (escroquerie fiscale) punishable by imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years and fines up to EUR 250,000, in addition to civil liability of the partners. The AEDT applies risk-based audits targeting carbon offset brokerage and cross-border service models, may request full partner-level documentation, and will deny input VAT recovery on any invalid or missing invoices; joint and several payment liability can extend to the general partner (gérant) of the SCSp.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) jointly provide central banking and prudential supervision; BCL executes monetary policy within the Eurosystem, while CSSF licenses and supervises credit institutions and payment services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is legal tender; Luxembourg maintains full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under EU Treaty provisions (TFEU Art. 63), with no foreign-exchange controls, no surrender requirements, and no profit repatriation hurdles. Outbound/inbound payments require only standard banking documentation and, where applicable, tax reportable-category codes, not regulatory license. Capital-account conversion is unrestricted even for investment fund vehicles such as the SCSp.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg has no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts and service revenues (including ESG auditing and carbon offset brokerage fees) may be freely held, converted, or repatriated in any currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions are legally viable as payment-service providers for an SCSp only if they hold a valid passport/licence under PSD2 and are registered with the CSSF. Principal account and capital escrow should be at a Tier-1 Luxembourg credit institution; offshore EMIs outside the EEA will normally be judged 'Medium-to-Low' viability because they cannot provide collateral-grade escrow, sub-custody, or trade finance instruments, and are often rejected for anti-money-laundering comfort by downstream investors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML/CFT rules do not impose a blanket physical appearance requirement; remote onboarding is permitted for Low_Risk_Standard non-financial corporate clients if electronic identification (eIDAS trust services) or video identification with independent authentication is used. However, most Tier-1 domestic banks retain a compliance policy requiring at least one face-to-face meeting with the general partner's authorised signatories and the ultimate beneficial owners of the SCSp, especially where the partnership is newly formed and has no audited financial statement. A fully remote opening is possible at some digital-friendly institutions if the full documentary dossier is apostilled/legalised and source-of-wealth evidence is immaculate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unidentifiable ultimate beneficial owner chain caused by LP interests or held-through partnerships.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current RCS extract of SCSp, full partnership agreement (LPA), an UBO registry filing (RBE register extract), an up-to-date ownership/control org chart to natural persons, and, for each material UBO, passport copy plus residence proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Origin of capital injection and incoming wires from non-transparent trust or offshore holding structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-to-bank custody chain, source-of-wealth report with income/asset documentation, and sworn statement of origin of funds signed by the general partner and each LP contributing capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through tax classification perceived as a tax evasion or reporting-arbitrage red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax legal opinion (cabinet d'avocats), draft Form 100/202 filing calendar, compliance undertaking, and a copy of the Luxembourg income tax query/classification request if filed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanction/PEP screening hit on director, shareholder, or counterparty in the carbon offset value chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU/UN/OFAC sanctions screening report, PEP determination letter, negative news check, and evidence of the counterparty's independent compliance due diligence (KYC pack).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial rationale opaque for corporate Scope 1–3 carbon footprint auditing and offset brokerage fees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed ESG advisory services contract or master service agreement, invoices, engagement letters, and a work programme showing fees for agreed carbon accounting audit deliverables.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions are routed through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 (for interbank transmissions) into the SCSp's EUR IBAN account at a CSSF-licensed Luxembourg credit institution. The remittance instruction must clearly reference the share-class subscriber, the purpose code for 'Direct investment in the reporting economy' (e.g., EU BOP code D31 or ECB purpose description 'EQUI' for equity capital), and the corresponding investment contract. For amounts above EUR 10,000, the bank's AML engine will require a copy of the unit subscription form, the capital account statement reflecting the LP commitment, and a board/general partner resolution confirming the injection is a partnership capital contribution rather than a loan.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for international suppliers and carbon-offset counterparties are cleared through (i) SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR payments within EU/EEA, (ii) SWIFT MT103 for global low-value trade disbursements, (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) for documentary guarantee-based settlements, and (iv) TARGET2 for large-value euro interbank clearing. Non-EUR invoices are channelled in underlying trade currency with FX prior to payment, or settled via MT103 in the invoice currency and booked with an FX swap error account, subject to the bank's Standard Settlement Instructions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla Over-the-Counter FX Forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (dual-currency liability hedging)
European-style FX Options (call and put, vanilla)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) against non-convertible currencies of carbon-offset suppliers, provided a genuine hedging rationale and an ISDA/CSA master agreement are in place
Commodity/carbon credit forwards through regulated brokers if the physical offset is priced in a non-EUR unit

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (bilan et compte de profits et pertes) – required only if the SCSp exceeds the legal audit-exemption threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end (typically 30 June for a calendar-year SCSp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-imposed fine (amende) of EUR 500–5,000 and publication of judgment; persistent default may lead to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (RBE) – including updates to the partnership-interest register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RBE – Register of Beneficial Owners (held by Luxembourg Business Registers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 15 days after any qualifying change; rolling annual confirmation recommended at each 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EUR 125 to EUR 5,000 per non-compliant entity; possible criminal sanctions for the general partner/manager for deliberate omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership income tax declaration (nil or actual) for the pass-through SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the following fiscal year; extension to 31 December via eSpace
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 0.6% per commenced month of tax due (minimum EUR 50); discretionary assessment if return is not filed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if an SCSp exceeds two of the three thresholds: total assets > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average employees > 50. Audit may also be required by the partnership agreement or by CSSF rules for deemed-managed AIFs.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 as amended); IFRS voluntarily permitted for the partnership financial statements if elected under the same law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no separate standalone annual UBO return under Luxembourg law. Any transfer of partnership interests requires a transfer agreement, and the updated beneficial-ownership information must be filed with the RBE within 15 days. As market practice, the registered agent performs an annual KYC/UBO confirmation to certify that the RBE record remains accurate and current.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is tax-transparent with no entity-level CIT; qualifying IP income benefits from the Luxembourg IP Box (80% income exemption, approximate effective 5.16% CIT on qualifying IP royalty income); standard preferential deductions include the notional interest deduction on new equity and investment tax credit for small businesses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 500 (Corporate Income Tax and Municipal Business Tax Return); filed electronically via the Luxembourg tax administration portal 'XML-File' or through MyGuichet.lu / Guichet.lu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Deadline is 30 June following the fiscal year-end in the ordinary calendar; the Luxembourg tax administration routinely grants an extended filing deadline to 31 December, with further postponement possible upon written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the legal form and tax classification of the taxpayer; for an SCSp this confirms partnership pass-through status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should identify themselves as indirect taxpayers through the partnership and state the applicable DTA residence jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after correction for the SCSp's pass-through allocations to partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must record only allocable taxable income attributable to the Luxembourg source and any Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Notional interest deduction and other preferential deductions claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Luxembourg-resident corporate partners may claim NID; non-resident partners without a Luxembourg PE should leave blank.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing adjustments, including intercompany services, management fees, and cost-sharing transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled partners must disclose related-party dealings and arm's length benchmarks, subject to minimal threshold exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax reclaim or treaty relief claim indicator for outbound distributions to non-resident partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must certify Luxembourg tax residence and attach a TRC to claim DTA relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a penalty up to EUR 10,000 and an increase of up to 10% of the assessed tax; late payment of corporate income tax and municipal business tax triggers automatic monthly interest of 1% on overdue amounts, plus administrative fines for deliberate omissions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Resident partners and non-resident partners may invoke treaty relief by submitting a certificate of Luxembourg tax residence (Form 23) and the relevant DTA article via the MyGuichet.lu portal; the SCSp must provide a partner-by-partner allocation schedule, and withholding tax at domestic rate is withheld at distribution unless a valid tax residency certificate and, if requested, an advance tax ruling validate the exemption or reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties is 33.33% (4-year catch-all subject to 20% effective where recipient is resident of an EU/EEA state) but generally reduced to 0% for royalties under EU interest & royalty directive and treaties; statutory interest WHT is 0% for non-resident recipients, while interest paid to Luxembourg individual non-resident taxpayers may be subject to 20% WHT under the Savings Directive implemented domestically; treaties frequently reduce these rates further.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies OECD-aligned transfer pricing principles grounded in Article 56 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law; the SCSp must reflect real economic substance in respect of management, employees, premises, and decision-making; the Luxembourg implementation of the EU Economic Substance Requirements through the ATAD and domestic anti-abuse rules requires sufficient substance to avoid treaty denial under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) and controlled foreign company (CFC) rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of taxable distributions or under-declaration of SCSp income attributable to partners, use of fraudulent invoices for ESG carbon offset claims without offset delivery, or creation of artificial intercompany fee structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty of up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years; tax evasion surcharge of 20% to 100% of the evaded tax; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 per infraction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partner are jointly and severally liable for the entity's unpaid taxes if they signed a false return; travel bans and asset freezing orders may be imposed; civil restitution for the full tax deficiency and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp operates with zero employees, no Luxembourg bank account or substance, and undertakes no real management activity in Luxembourg while routing carbon credit brokerage income tax-neutrally to non-resident partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax transparency and treaty benefits; additional assessment at 24.94% CIT on the deemed taxable income; administrative penalty up to EUR 250,000; mandatory re-registration or disqualification for tax-abusive structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partner and directors can be held personally liable for the full CIT and municipal business tax assessed on the entity; court-imposed travel bans and removal from Luxembourg business registries possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of the SCSp to launder proceeds from fraudulent carbon credit schemes, duplicate offset credits, or offering carbon offsets without verified retirement in an internationally recognized registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML Law of 12 November 2004 penalties include imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of EUR 1,250 to EUR 500,000; confiscation of proceeds; regulatory fines imposed by the CSSF or Luxembourg public prosecutor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly involved in money laundering face personal criminal liability, imprisonment up to 5 years, and civil damages; travel bans and asset seizures are standard enforcement tools.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp sells carbon offset brokerage services to a related non-resident entity at a margin unsupported by comparables, charges excessive administrative fees to the Luxembourg partnership, or fails to maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A transfer pricing adjustor assessing arm's length profit at 24.94% CIT plus 1% monthly late-payment interest; penalty of up to 25% of the adjustment; 10% non-filing penalty and EUR 10,000 late documentation penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or approved non-arm's length transfer pricing can be jointly liable for the recovered tax; criminal liability for falsification of accounts; travel ban and restitution of lost corporate taxes may be imposed.
